sources.title: Tatarica: the Kazan Khanate
sources.note: Scholarly Tatar Encyclopedia: foundation1438 or1445, Middle Volga/Kama, population,1552 conquest and resistance until1557, continuity. October used without questionable source calendar conversion.

sources.title: UNESCO: Historic and Architectural Complex of the Kazan Kremlin
sources.note: Brief synthesis and criteria: capital political/military/administrative/commercial/cultural functions; present16th-to19th-century ensemble incorporates earlier remains. No attribution of modern Kul Sharif Mosque to a surviving khanate structure.

sources.title: I. L. Izmaylov, Tatarica: Suyumbike
sources.note: Biography, regency1549to1551 for young Utyamysh Giray after Safa Giray died; deposition and mother/son sent Moscow11August1551. Unsupported superlative among first Muslim women rulers omitted; no tower suicide legend.

sources.title: Tatarica: the peasantry
sources.note: Thirteenth-to-mid-sixteenth-century rural section: rye/oats/barley/millet/buckwheat, tools; Kazan-period leather/woodwork/spinning/weaving and specialists. Broad chronological synthesis labelled; later Russian-period household statistics not imported.

sources.title: Tatarica: art of the Kazan Khanate
sources.note: Archaeological finds at Kazan Kremlin and Iske Kazan: glazed/wheel-made pots and inkwells, animal-headed kumgans, embossed or silk-embroidered leather footwear, architectural alabaster arabesque panels. Kazan crown uncertain provenance omitted.

sources.title: Tatarica: bakyrche, the coppersmith
sources.note: Historical opening: medieval kumgans and unique brass wine pitcher in bird form, late15th-to-early16th-century Nasyr named as Emin Khan coppersmith. Later village production not backdated.

sources.title: National Museum of the Republic of Tatarstan: the tarhan charter
sources.note: Museum object record,1523 Sahib Giray grant: specified beneficiaries exempt tax, forced lodging, gifts to envoys, food/fodder and land taxes, protection of property. Avoid absolute claim only surviving khanate document.

sources.title: I. A. Mustakimov: the Kazan charter of Khan Sahib Giray, 2013
sources.note: Srednevekovye tyurko-tatarskie gosudarstva5, pp31to47. Printed41/PDF40 charter1Jan1523=13Safar929, original NMRT5757; printed43/PDF42 Arabic seal transcription and Russian translation. Original host unavailable, identical full scholarly volume read via https://royalhouseofsiberia.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/04/sttg_5.pdf and cached sttg5.pdf. seal-edition-p43.png visually checked. Two unbracketed words only, modern transcription.

sources.title: Tatarica: Muhammadyar
sources.note: Works section: Tuhfa-i mardan1539to1540 and Nur-i sudur1542; justice, honesty, peace, generosity and moral duties of rulers. Literary ideals not proof of actual universal fairness.

sources.title: M. A. Usmanov, Tatarica: archaeographic expeditions
sources.note: History opening: Arabic/Persian/Turkic-Tatar manuscript collections in Golden Horde and Tatar khanates, mosque/medrese libraries; specifically large collection at principal Kazan mosque. No universal literacy rate asserted.

sources.title: I. L. Izmaylov and S. Yu. Izmaylova: Sahib Giray’s charter
sources.note: Study section:1912 Vakhidi located document at Mamalayevo with farmer Rakhmatulla Akhmarov who kept it as healing talisman;1920 acquired for museum. Clearly modern afterlife, not medieval efficacy claim. Entry919Hijri typo not repeated; scholarly edition establishes929.
